On the other hand, radiative extinction can be important in microgravity and its improved understanding s hould contribute to spacecraft fire safety. Microgravity experiments allowed the first obser vation of radiative extinction, this being for droplet combustion (Dietrich et al., 1996, Nayagam et al., 1998). Santa et al. (2007a) presents observations of radiative extinction in gaseous spherical flames. As described above, the experiments were conducted in microgravity in the NASA Glenn 2.2 s drop tower.

sources.text: CFI document Reports_CFI Science Final Report, page 9: Cool flame extinction diameters as a function of ambient pressure for n-dodecane droplets burning in air. Since the cool flame extinction is an instability phenomenon where the dynamic balance between heat release and heat loss from the flame is lost at the lower turning point in the NTC region, one would expect addition of helium to have a substantial influence on the process. Figure 5 illustrates the effect of helium dilution on the extinction diameter for n-dodecane. Increase helium dilution leads to earlier cool flame extinction giving a larger extinction diameter.
